item: Row 424: the import's keyword-counter reconcile checks only the keywords the imported articles mention, and every reconcile rewrites only the counters that were wrong
summary: keyword_counter_reconcile was the largest post-swap cost after the junk scan (18.3 s of a 72 s import on lane O's bench; 30 s of lane S's 212 s restore). Two changes. (1) reconcile_keyword_counters zeroed and rewrote every keyword row per slice, one UPDATE each, although almost all were already right; it now stamps the slice with one range UPDATE and rewrites only the rows its drift scan found wrong (same end state row for row, and no reader can see a zeroed keyword); the GROUP BY runs before the write gate and, under it, every row whose stored counters disagree with it is read again before anything is written, so an ingest that commits between the two is never undone (Plan's check; pinned by a test that injects an ingest at exactly that point and fails when the stale GROUP BY is trusted). Holding the gate across the GROUP BY instead was measured at a 2.9 s ingest stall on the 186k + 122k store; the longest hold is now 273 ms for the sweep and 36 ms for the scoped pass, against 908 ms on main. (2) New reconcile_keyword_counters_for_articles recomputes exactly the keywords the swap group's imported articles mention, with the sweep's arithmetic (all live unquarantined mentions, R101) and stamp; keywords it does not touch keep counters and stamp, so the envelope still discloses older drift. reconcile_counters_after_import (called by the import stage) uses it when the group is derived and the import is under a quarter of the corpus, then runs the budgeted insurance sweep inside what is left of the same budget unless the counters are exact AND a whole sweep landed within the freshness window: the envelope reads only keywords above 0, so a keyword stored at 0 over real mentions (pre-2026-07-29 drift) is invisible to it, and the sweep now records when its oldest slice of the last whole pass was verified (derived_meta counter_reconcile_swept_at, written only when a sweep reaches the end and carrying the time it BEGAN, so a stopped or budget-cut sweep is never insurance; found by the independent read, tightened by Plan). Measured on 4 CPUs, plaintext synthetic stores (Zipf keywords, 60 per article): 3,000 articles into 300,000 with the corpus swept within the window, 13.75 s to 3.22 s; never swept, 16.32 s to 12.22 s; 122,000 into 186,000 (the sweep route), 10.26 s to 5.54 s (a second run of main gave 11.46 s). Pinned by a mixed golden case, 24 random corpora against the whole-corpus sweep, 6 corpora whose expected keywords come from the generator rather than the gathering query, behavioural tests of every route and of the budget handoff, a real carried import (no drift to repair, identical to the sweep) and a source pin of the stage's branches. kw engine pin kept with --same.
